[FPMC](https://www.iw3c2.org/papers/2025-Factorizing-Personalized-Markov-Chains.pdf) combines user–item preference with factorized item transitions; [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) combines historical item similarity with personalized higher-order Markov dynamics. [SDM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.00385) establishes learned gating between short- and long-term representations. Thus, combining persistent and recent interests, asymmetric transitions, and adaptive fusion have precedents. The proposed score adds a context-gated, low-rank transition residual to SASRec. Here h already captures recent and longer dependencies; calling it purely “long-term” is unjustified. Averaging three embeddings makes r order-insensitive within that window. These connections support an incremental architectural interpretation, not an originality claim.

Recommended controls: original SASRec; fixed gates g=0, 0.5, 1; a learned global scalar sigmoid(a); and the context-dependent scalar MLP gate. Retrain each with identical data, optimization, validation selection, and comparable tuning budgets. Compare against SASRec with an equally sized scoring MLP or residual adapter to control extra capacity. For directionality, compare M=AᵀB against a symmetric, potentially indefinite factorization M=QᵀDQ with signed diagonal D, matching rank and parameter budget as closely as possible. AᵀA alone also imposes positive semidefiniteness, confounding symmetry. Gate shuffling across validation contexts tests whether routing assignments matter.

Gate magnitude alone cannot measure reliance: projection scale can compensate for gate scale, and factor scales are non-identifiable. Measure the realized residual c_j=g rᵀMe_j: candidate-centered RMS relative to the base branch, positive–negative margin contributions, branch correlation, and rank/top-10 changes. Report paired macro-validation HR@10 changes when removing the residual or replacing/shuffling gates at inference. Distinguish these intervention effects from retrained ablations; neither establishes causal user preferences.
